In a biological network where nodes represent proteins and edges represent physical interactions, a specific node [IMAGE: /data/images/bt4002_2026T1_ET_AN_p1_Im3.webp|inline] has a very high betweenness centrality but a relatively low degree centrality. What is the most likely biological role of this protein?
options: It is a global hub protein that interacts with almost every other protein in the cell.
It is a redundant protein that can be removed without affecting the network diameter.
It is a peripheral protein located at the end of a signalling cascade.
It acts as a bottleneck or bridge between two distinct functional modules.
questions.correct_answer: It acts as a bottleneck or bridge between two distinct functional modules.

questions.text: Which of the following is true about genome assembly?

questions.text: Which information is lost or distorted after projecting a Drug-Target bipartite network into a Drug- Drug network?
options: Information regarding targets that were only connected to a single drug (leaf nodes in the bipartite graph).
The topological distance (path length) between two drugs in the drug-drug space.
The specific identity of the target proteins shared between drugs.
The degree of 'overlap' (multiplicity) of targets between two drugs.
correct_answer: Information regarding targets that were only connected to a single drug (leaf nodes in the bipartite graph).
The specific identity of the target proteins shared between drugs.
